open_points.subject: OperationBinding after manifest digest drift and reversion
open_points.text: K-03 says invocation is refused “until a new binding is accepted,” while M10 says invocation checks whether the manifest record “still has the pinned digest,” and State 1 deliberately carries no binding-drift history.
open_points.question: If the manifest operation changes and later returns exactly to the binding’s pinned digest, does the existing accepted binding become invocable again, or does the earlier mismatch permanently require a newly accepted binding?
options: The existing binding works again whenever the current digest equals its pin
Once any mismatch has been observed, the binding remains unusable until a new binding is accepted
open_points.default_guess: The existing binding works again whenever the current digest equals its pin, because no drift state is modeled.

open_points.subject: Accepting an already accepted OperationBinding after its service loses its selected instance
open_points.text: State 0 says “an accepted one is returned whatever the manifest says now,” while M28 says that for a service with no selected instance “a binding for it is refused when proposed or accepted.”
open_points.question: When the owner repeats accept on an already accepted binding after the installation no longer selects an instance for its service, is the accepted binding returned or is the action refused?
options: Refuse because the service currently has no selected instance
open_points.default_guess: Return the already accepted binding, while refusing its invocation.

open_points.subject: try an implementation
open_points.text: The action promises “trial evidence per case,” while M07 models one TrialExecution for one implementation and one trial case; the text never says which cases an explicit try action runs.
open_points.question: Which TrialCases does one explicit try-an-implementation action execute?
options: Every case currently in the contract version’s corpus
A caller-selected subset of existing cases
Caller-supplied ad hoc inputs that need not be TrialCases
open_points.default_guess: Every case currently in the contract version’s corpus.

open_points.subject: EffectAttempt resume after not_sent
open_points.text: M26 says “A `not_sent` attempt leaves its approval unused (M24), so a resume sends a new attempt under it,” but M26 also says an attempt may instead use a standing grant or, for an initial `draft-write`, a flow activation.
open_points.question: What authority does the resumed send use when a `not_sent` attempt originally used a standing grant or a flow activation rather than an approval?
options: Reuse the original authority regardless of its current state
Re-evaluate normal authority at resume time: retain an unused exact approval, require an active grant, and use the run’s original flow activation for draft-write
Require a fresh owner approval for every resumed non-read send
open_points.default_guess: Re-evaluate normal authority at resume time, retaining an unused exact approval, honoring only a still-active grant, and using the run’s original flow activation for an initial draft-write.
